text.en: These Regulations may be cited as the Intoxicating Substances (Treatment and Rehabilitation) Regulations. Interpretation.

In these Regulations, unless the context otherwise requires — “Director” means the Director of the Narcotics Control Bureau; “medical officer” means a Government medical officer who for the time being is assigned to perform the functions of a medical officer under these Regulations; “officer-in-charge” means a person appointed by the Minister under section 19(2) to be the officer-in-charge of an approved institution. Supervision and control of approved institution.

(1) Subject to any direction of the Minister, an approved institution shall be under the general charge and supervision of the Director.

(2) Subject to any direction of the Director, the officer-in-charge of an approved institution shall be responsible for the occupation, discipline and control of the residents and may issue general orders which shall be observed by the residents. Medical examination.
Every resident shall be examined by a medical officer as soon as possible after his admission to an approved institution. 4 CAP. 161, Rg 2 Intoxicating Substances Bedding and diet.

Every resident of an approved institution shall —

(a) be provided with a separate bed; and

(b) be supplied with sufficient and varied food based in a dietary scale drawn up by the medical officer and approved by the Director. Daily routine.

The daily routine of every resident in an approved institution, including the hours of sleep and recreation of, and classroom instruction, practical training, domestic work and meals given to, such resident shall be in accordance with a scheme approved, from time to time, by the Director. Vocational training.

The vocational training given to residents shall, insofar as is practicable, be directed towards preparing them for some form of employment, having regard to the capacity, aptitude and preference of each resident. Reasonable recreation etc.

No resident in an approved institution shall be employed to work in the approved institution in such a way as to impair the residents capacity to acquire any knowledge or skill from the education or training given therein or to deprive the resident of reasonable recreation or leisure. Religious instruction.
So far as is practicable, arrangements shall be made for the religious instruction of residents according to their own religious persuasion.
